source: Ported from playon/pulse Pulse.Web/scripts (Test-NetworkDomains, Test-NetworkPorts, Test-TlsInspection). Port list audited against Canopy connections.csv.
notes: Zixi streaming goes to a broadcaster assigned per event from AWS pools, not to prod-echo. Allow UDP 443/2088 by port, not by destination IP.

Streaming failover chain: Zixi UDP/2088 -> Zixi UDP/443 -> RTMP TCP/1935. Either UDP path alone is a healthy stream; RTMP is a degraded last resort. Each streaming probe's "path" names its place in the chain, and the probes are listed in chain order.

balena-cloud.com hosts come from Balena's published list (https://api.balena-cloud.com/os/v1/network-endpoints, checked 2026-10-30). Balena says the list can change; *.balena-cloud.com on TCP 443 is their recommended rule. vpn.balena-cloud.com no longer resolves; cloudlink replaced it.

severityLevels.comment: From the NFHS article's impact ratings. Any critical or high failure makes the verdict Not ready. medium failures and warnings give Ready with issues.

services.name: Live streaming
services.blocked: The broadcast cannot reach the streaming servers, or starts late on a fallback path.

services.name: Event scheduling and viewing
services.blocked: Events cannot be scheduled and viewers cannot watch.

services.name: Pixellot cloud and updates
services.blocked: The Pixellot cannot be managed or receive software updates.

services.name: Scoreboard graphics
services.blocked: Scoreboard graphics and watermarks will not appear on the broadcast.

services.name: Remote support
services.blocked: Support cannot connect to the Pixellot to diagnose or fix it.

services.name: Clock sync
services.blocked: The Pixellot's clock can drift, and it may miss scheduled events.

services.name: Name lookups (DNS)
services.blocked: The Pixellot cannot look up any of its services.

speedTest.comment: Minimum from docUrl: 10 Mbps upload and download. Uses Cloudflare's public speed-test endpoints (no key). __down returns 403 above about 50 MB (checked 2026-10-30).

requirements.comment: What IT is asked to allow, from docUrl (2026-08-18), one row per firewall rule. Every rule is outbound from the Pixellot. Each probe below names the rule it tests in ruleId; a rule no probe names is shown as not tested. The report and its CSV are built from this list.

rules.purpose: Name lookups. The Pixellot uses 8.8.8.8 by default.
rules.note: If your network forces internal DNS, request a DNS change for the unit at help.nfhsnetwork.com.

rules.purpose: Pixellot cloud, management and software updates
rules.note: If your firewall can't use wildcard domains, allow the domain in the web filter or as a URL category (these match the HTTPS server name), or use the current IP addresses listed in this report.

rules.purpose: NFHS Network event scheduling and viewing
rules.note: If your firewall can't use wildcard domains, allow the domain in the web filter or as a URL category (these match the HTTPS server name), or use the current IP addresses listed in this report.
If your firewall can't use wildcard domains, allow UDP 2088 to any destination from the Pixellot. Streaming servers change every event, so a list of IP addresses goes out of date.
If your firewall can't use wildcard domains, allow UDP 443 to any destination from the Pixellot. Streaming servers change every event, so a list of IP addresses goes out of date.
The RTMP servers (*.pixellot.stream) exist only during events, so allow the port to any destination.
If your firewall can't use wildcard domains, allow UDP 123 to any destination from the Pixellot.
If your firewall can't use wildcard domains, allow the domain in the web filter or as a URL category (these match the HTTPS server name), or use the current IP addresses listed in this report.
If your firewall can't use wildcard domains, allow the domain in the web filter or as a URL category (these match the HTTPS server name), or use the current IP addresses listed in this report.

rules.purpose: Management and updates for Linux (balenaOS) units
rules.note: If your firewall can't use wildcard domains, allow the domain in the web filter or as a URL category (these match the HTTPS server name), or use the current IP addresses listed in this report.

rules.purpose: Remote management tunnel for Linux (balenaOS) units
rules.note: OpenVPN, not HTTPS, so web filters can't match it by name. Allow its current IP addresses, and don't block OpenVPN by application ID.

ports.rule: Allow outbound UDP 53 to 8.8.8.8, the Pixellot's default DNS server. If your network forces internal DNS, request a DNS change for the unit at help.nfhsnetwork.com.
Allow outbound UDP 123 (NTP) to *.pixellot.tv. The Pixellot checks its clock against prod-echo.pixellot.tv.

Allow outbound UDP 2088 to *.pixellot.stream and *.pixellot.tv. Streaming servers are assigned per event from changing cloud addresses, so use domain rules, not IP addresses. prod-echo.pixellot.tv is the Pixellot's own port test, which is what this check uses.
ports.consequence: Primary streaming path. If only this is blocked, the stream falls back to UDP 443, then to RTMP (TCP 1935), which starts about 4 minutes late.

ports.rule: Allow outbound UDP 443 to *.pixellot.stream and *.pixellot.tv. Streaming servers are assigned per event from changing cloud addresses, so use domain rules, not IP addresses. prod-echo.pixellot.tv is the Pixellot's own port test, which is what this check uses.
ports.consequence: Backup streaming path, used when UDP 2088 is blocked. If both are blocked, the stream falls back to RTMP (TCP 1935).

ports.rule: Allow outbound TCP 1935 to any destination. The RTMP fallback servers (*.pixellot.stream) exist only during events, so a rule limited to them cannot be tested ahead of time, by you or by this check. This check connects to a public RTMP server (a.rtmp.youtube.com), which a port rule lets through.
ports.consequence: Last-resort streaming path. If UDP 2088, UDP 443 and this are all blocked, the broadcast never goes on air.

ports.rule: Allow outbound TCP 443 to cloudlink.balena-cloud.com. It is OpenVPN, not HTTPS: SNI/hostname filters cannot see it, so allow its resolved IPs, and exempt it from SSL inspection and application-ID blocking of OpenVPN.

patternNote: SSL inspection bypass lists match by pattern. Exempting app.singular.live or *.app.singular.live does not cover datastream.singular.live, so exempt the whole *.singular.live (and each domain listed) rather than individual hosts.

notTested.why: Streaming servers are created for each event and do not exist between events. This tool tests the same ports against prod-echo.pixellot.tv instead.
Only needed at sites with SportzCast scoreboard hardware.

notTested.item: HTTP CONNECT through a web proxy
notTested.why: Only relevant if outbound HTTPS must go through an explicit proxy.

notTested.item: Rate limits and internet sleep schedules
notTested.why: Policies that apply only to the Pixellot's address or at certain hours are not visible from this computer.
